description: Team trillium is a solo entry by Graham Mefford, Duke ‘30 (Economics + Mathematics). For the Earth System Trend Detective challenge, I use NASA MERRA-2 reanalysis to measure 45 years of 2 m air temperature change over the Southeast US (1980 to 2025). Monthly and annual series feed a linear trend per decade, tested for statistical significance, so real warming is separated from year-to-year noise. It brings quant-style rigor to Earth data, distilled into figures anyone can read in seconds.
summary:
Trillium is an Earth System Trend Detective for the Southeast United States. We pulled 549 monthly NASA MERRA-2 granules (M2TMNXSLV, 1980–2025) and built an open Python pipeline that answers the challenge's four questions: what, where, how much, and is it significant?

The answer: 2 m air temperature is rising +0.29 °C per decade (95% CI 0.20–0.37), about +1.3 °C since 1980 and roughly 1.4× the global rate (GISTEMP v4). Every grid cell is warming, and 97% remain significant after Benjamini–Hochberg false-discovery control. Winters are warming 2.2× faster than summers, and the fastest warming is in the Carolina Piedmont near Charlotte. The trend holds under Mann–Kendall, Sen's slope, OLS, bootstrap, and autocorrelation-corrected tests (Hamed–Rao p ≈ 1e-6). We also caught and fixed a partial-year bias that had inflated the trend by 9%.

Results are presented in an interactive web brief with warming stripes, a year-by-year map with playback, a monthly anomaly heatmap, and a plain-language verdict.

This matters because the Southeast's growing cities, farms, and power grids need local evidence, not just global averages. Trillium turns raw NASA data into findings anyone can check and reuse.
details:
WHAT IT DOES / HOW IT WORKS

Trillium is an end-to-end pipeline that turns raw NASA reanalysis data into a tested climate finding. It downloads 549 monthly MERRA-2 granules (M2TMNXSLV, 2 m air temperature, 1980–2025) for the Southeast US box (-84,30 to -75,37) through NASA Earthdata/earthaccess. It then:

1. Area-averages the data and builds annual series from complete calendar years only.

2. Tests the trend with OLS, Mann–Kendall, Sen's slope, a 2,000-resample bootstrap, and autocorrelation-corrected Mann–Kendall (Hamed–Rao, Yue–Wang, pre-whitened).

3. Runs the same tests on every grid cell, with Benjamini–Hochberg false-discovery control.

4. Splits the trend by season, finds change-points (PELT), and computes signal-to-noise and time of emergence.

5. Compares the Southeast with the global record (GISTEMP v4).

One command regenerates every number, figure, the report, the website data, and the 30-second video.

BENEFITS & IMPACT

Result: +0.29 °C/decade (95% CI 0.20–0.37), about 1.4× the global rate. 100% of grid cells are warming, 97% pass the false-discovery test, winters warm 2.2× faster than summers, and the Carolina Piedmont warms fastest. City planners, farmers, utilities, and students get a local, statistically defensible answer they can explore in a browser, check, and reuse for other regions or variables.

TOOLS

Python (xarray, pandas, NumPy, SciPy, statsmodels, pymannkendall, ruptures, matplotlib, earthaccess), pytest, ffmpeg; React, TypeScript, Vite, Leaflet, Recharts, Framer Motion; Netlify hosting.

CREATIVITY

Every visual comes from the real data: warming stripes form the page background, a "time machine" map replays each year since 1980, and a heatmap shows every month as a cell. The 30-second video is rendered frame by frame from the analysis itself, with no stock or AI footage.

FACTORS WE CONSIDERED

Scientific honesty came first. We caught and fixed a bug in which a partial year (Jan–Sep 2025, missing the cool months) inflated the trend by 9%, and added automated tests so it can't return. Climate data is autocorrelated, so we used corrected significance tests. Testing hundreds of grid cells invites false positives, so we applied FDR control. MERRA-2 is a reanalysis that can't resolve neighborhood-scale heat, so we state that limitation openly. Accessibility drove a plain-language four-question verdict alongside the full statistics.
